newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: REITH SAYS NO DISAGREEMENT WITH PM ON MINIMUM WAGE
The Federal Industrial Relations Minister, Peter Reith, says he has no difference of opinion with the Prime Minister, on the issue of a minimum wage.
John Howard said yesterday one of the reasons Australia's unemployment rate was higher than that of the United States was because it had higher minimum wages compared to countries like the US.
He called for a national debate on the minimum wage, while Reith was reported as saying increased productivity was the key to solving unemployment.
Mr Reith said Mr Howard was not advocating a lowering, or the removal, of the minimum wage.
He said the Prime Minister was just pointing out the differences between the Australian and American systems, which could explain the difference in their respective unemployment rates.
"That is not however saying that we ought to be reducing or changing the basic framework of the system we have in Australia, he said.
GOLD COMPANIES RECOUPING WITH RISE IN SHARE INDEX
Gold companies are this morning recouping some of the many millions of dollars wiped off their value.

The gold share index has risen 2.8 percent in the first hour of trade, arresting massive share price falls experienced since Friday, when the Reserve Bank announced that it had sold two-thirds of its bullion assets.
The price of gold is also up a little.
Gold's currently selling for US$319.20 an ounce, almost a dollar higher than yesterday's Sydney close.
GOVERNMENT AND RESERVE BANK ACCUSED OF "ECONOMIC VANDALISM"
The Reserve Bank and the Federal Government have been accused of economic vandalism over the crisis facing the gold industry.
New South Wales Mineral Resources Minister, Bob Martin, says $1 billion worth of gold projects in the state are now in doubt because of the slump in prices.
Gold prices plummetted to a 12-year low after the Reserve Bank announced last Friday that it had sold two-thirds of its bullion reserves.
Mr Martin says Prime Minister John Howard and Treasurer Peter Costello, have given the nod to vandalise Australia's gold reserves and drive the price of gold below the cost of production.
He says the decision shows gross irresponsibility which reeks of bottom line economics and fails to look after Australia's second most important export earner.
The Reserve Bank has declined to comment on recent criticisms of its action.
TRIBUNAL ON ALLEGED SECRET DOCUMENTS ON HOLSWORTHY SITE
Allegations that the Federal Government has kept secret documents from the public about the Holsworthy airport proposal, will go before the Administrative Appeals Tribunal next month.

The CRASH group, which is made up of seven councils and 13 community groups in Sydney's south, has accused the government of refusing to give details of the proposal, under Freedom of Information legislation.
Chairperson, Councillor Lorraine Rodden, said the group wants to know why Holsworthy has been resurrected as a site for Sydney's second airport.
NSW CAMBODIAN LEADER CALLS FOR EVACUATION OF AUSTRALIANS
The Cambodian Community has called on the Federal Government to evacuate Australians trapped in Cambodia before fighting between the warring political factions intensifies.
President of the NSW Kmher Community, Pore Heang Ya, says the Australian Government should not wait until hostilities worsen before taking action to get Australians out of Cambodia.
He says the fact other countries are acting urgently to get nationals out is evidence enough to move now.
Pore Heang Ya says those countries must hold grave fears that the fighting will intensify in the next few days.
He says if that is the case, Australia should do the same.
APPEAL DISMISSED IN LANDMARK FAMILY COURT CASE
The full bench of the Family Court has dismissed an appeal by a father who wanted to stop his former wife from moving to another state with his children.
Both the Federal Attorney General and the Human Rights Commission intervened in the landmark case.
The man appealed a trial judge's decision last year which allowed the woman to move from Cairns to Benidgo in Victoria, where she intended to marry.
He objected on the grounds that judge erred in allowing the woman's desires to have precedent over the rights of children.
The mother contended that her submission was supported by the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child.
The full bench of the Family Court ruled that that judge had properly considered the background of the case and the impact of the move on the children, and dismissed the appeal.
COAL BEING SENT FROM OTHER MINES TO COMBAT STRIKE

In New South Wales, management of the Hunter Valley number One mine has confirmed that coal is being sent from the company's other mines in the Hunter to fulfill contracts with the mine's overseas customers.
During the current strike, Rio Tinto has been exporting coal from the Howick and Mount Thorley mines to customers normally supplied from its Hunter Valley operation.
Over the past few weeks non-union staff have been mining coal from the Hunter Valley One mine and have attempted unsuccessfully to move a $12 million stockpile to the port of Newcastle.

Mine General Manager Allan Davies says the company still has to supply coal to its customers and to do so its been selling coal from two other Rio Tinto mines in the Upper Hunter. But Mr Davies says he does not want to continue doing this and would rather supply coal from Hunter Valley number One.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
